full-port-map.evidence: The authorized service farm may use high-numbered ports.
full-port-map.observation: Saved scan files and a web inventory containing the port token.

checkpoint.question: Why scan all TCP ports in this inventory task?
choices: A service may listen outside the common default port set.
All-port scans prove that every service is secure.
Port scanning reveals every application password.
checkpoint.explanation: Coverage matters: a default scan can miss a high-port listener. Open ports are findings, not proof of a vulnerability.

version-ledger.evidence: Your saved port map identifies listeners to inspect more closely.
version-ledger.observation: A versioned plain-text ledger banner and a version token.

checkpoint.question: Which observation is stronger than a port-name guess?
choices: The filename chosen for a scan report.
The actual banner returned by the listener.
checkpoint.explanation: A banner is observed service behavior; even banners can be misleading, so record it as evidence, not absolute identity.

http-metadata.evidence: The identified HTTP service exposes response headers as well as a body.
http-metadata.observation: The metadata token and objective flag appear in named HTTP headers.

checkpoint.question: Why inspect headers as well as the page body?
choices: HTTP headers are a kind of DNS record.
Headers can contain metadata that is absent from the body.
Headers are automatically more trustworthy than content.
checkpoint.explanation: Headers and body are distinct parts of the response. This task places its evidence in headers.

fingerprint-proof.evidence: Port, version and HTTP metadata tokens form your inventory evidence.
fingerprint-proof.observation: The final inventory endpoint accepts all three tokens.

checkpoint.question: Why preserve the scan output with the report?
choices: It lets you trace the report back to observations.
Saving output makes every version string accurate.
A saved report prevents future configuration changes.
checkpoint.explanation: Reproducible observations support your conclusion; saving them does not guarantee identity or freeze the target.
